translationRepairs: When Ziji came home, his son at six inherited the rank, lowered to duke.
His son Jigui, at age six, inherited the title, which was reduced to duke.
子冀歸 names the heir 冀歸 (Jigui); s0102’s 賜名稚 confirms this is a personal name, so “Ziji came home” invents a homecoming verb.
Ziji returned; at age six he inherited the title, which was reduced to duke.
His son Jigui, at age six, inherited the title, which was reduced to duke.
冀歸 is the personal name Jigui, not a return verb, but the proposed “His son Jigui;” is a sentence fragment; a full clause restores the name without the awkward break.
On Shizu's campaign against Helian Chang, Daosheng with Changsun Han, Minister of Works, and E Qing, Director of the Imperial Clan, led the van and brought the realm down.
On Shizu's campaign against Helian Chang, Daosheng with Changsun Han, Minister over the Masses, and E Qing, Director of the Imperial Clan, led the van and brought the realm down.
司徒長孫翰 marks Changsun Han’s office as 司徒 (Minister over the Masses), not 司空 (Minister of Works).
When Shizu campaigned against Helian Chang, Daosheng with Minister of Works Changsun Han and Director of the Imperial Clan E Qing served as vanguard and thereupon pacified the state.
When Shizu campaigned against Helian Chang, Daosheng with Minister over the Masses Changsun Han and Director of the Imperial Clan E Qing served as vanguard and thereupon pacified the state.
The same 司徒 in 司徒長孫翰 is Minister over the Masses; “Minister of Works” is the wrong office title.
He became director of the Masters of Writing, palace attendant, and concurrently minister of writing and grand mobile secretariat, still holding Chang'an.
He was transferred to Minister over the Masses, added attendant-in-ordinary, and concurrently Minister of Writing and grand mobile secretariat, still garrisoning Chang'an.
遷司徒公 is promotion to Minister over the Masses; 兼尚書令 is the concurrent Masters-of-Writing post, so the before text misassigns 尚書令 to 司徒公.
He was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing, added Palace Attendant, and concurrently Minister of Writing and Grand Mobile Secretariat, still garrisoning Chang'an.
He was transferred to Minister over the Masses, added Palace Attendant, and concurrently Minister of Writing and Grand Mobile Secretariat, still garrisoning Chang'an.
Literal likewise reads 遷司徒公 as Masters of Writing; that title belongs to concurrent 尚書令, while 司徒公 is Minister over the Masses.
Zhi asked to pass the title to his cousin on his mother's side, Grand Minister of Justice Yuan Hongchao's second son Yun.
Zhi asked to transfer the enfeoffment to the second son Yun of his maternal cousin, Grand Minister of Justice Yuan Hongchao.
姨兄廷尉卿元洪超 identifies Hongchao as the maternal cousin, and 次子惲 is Hongchao’s second son; the before appositive makes Yun himself the cousin.
Thereupon he gave Luo's former husband's daughter, the Lu clan, in marriage, and married Xingde's elder brother Xingen to repay him.
Thereupon he married Luo's former husband's daughter of the Lu clan to Xingde's elder brother Xingen in order to repay him.
以…呂氏，妻興德兄興恩 means he married the Lu daughter to Xingen; the before splits this into two garbled marriage acts.
